subject: geography
title: Sussex Cell & Selsey Bill
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on Sussex sediment cell, Selsey Bill and managed realignment.
final_note: Sussex cell shows both hard and soft strategies.

concepts.def: Cell 4 from Selsey Bill east to Beachy Head.
Headland in West Sussex; rapidly retreating chalk and clay coast.
Managed realignment 2013 creating 183 ha intertidal habitat.
Tidal lagoon; SSSI nature reserve at northern end of cell.
162 m chalk cliff at eastern end of Sussex cell.
Sussex chalk cliffs retreat 30-100 cm/yr through wave undercutting and rockfall.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cell 4 runs from Selsey Bill to Beachy Head. Net longshore drift eastward. Chalk recession at Birling Gap reached 1 m/yr 2014-15 storms. Shingle accumulates at Brighton; groyne field maintains beach as defence and tourism asset.

Environment Agency breached 110 m sea wall in 2013, creating 183 ha intertidal habitat. £28 million scheme protects 348 homes from 1-in-1000 year flood. Habitat for migratory birds; oysters returning. Saved £90 million in defence costs over 100 years.

£10 million rock armour and sea wall protects 4500 homes including holiday parks. Bill (point) erodes 2 m/yr unprotected. Loss of Manhood Peninsula (becoming an island) possible without continued investment. Demonstrates value-based defence prioritisation.
